paper.abstract_en: The shapes and environments of cosmic structures carry cosmological information beyond the matter power spectrum. Recovering this information while retaining a physical understanding is a central challenge for cosmological inference. We construct an interpretable, rotation-equivariant neural marking scheme that reweights the matter field, combining learned density responses with explicit measures of local morphology. This approach enables direct inspection of the learned transformations, while retaining the advantages of a two-point function analysis. We employ a contrastive learning framework to align the marked summaries with the respective cosmological parameters. In real-space matter simulations, the learned marked spectra recover information beyond the ordinary power spectrum, tightening marginalized Fisher constraints on $σ_8$ and $Ω_m$ by factors of $1.7\times$ and $1.5\times$ relative to the power spectrum plus bispectrum at $k_{\mathrm{max}}=0.3\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Without retraining, our mark also improves a neutrino-mass forecast by a factor of $1.5\times$ relative to the power spectrum at the same scale cut. Across the cosmological prior, our marking scheme also improve the prediction errors in both parameters by $1.3\times$ over the best tested classical mark at $k_{\mathrm{max}}=0.2\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. A qualitative comparison with neural forecasts motivates the possibility that these different compressions approach a common information level. Neural marked statistics thus offer a route to extracting non-Gaussian information from cosmological surveys, combining interpretable, physically motivated transformations with the practical advantages of two-point estimators.
